final_answer.summary: EGFR is a highly viable, clinically validated target in lung cancer, especially EGFR-mutant NSCLC; it is not a general all-comers lung-cancer target.

target_entity.name: EGFR
target_entity.entity_type: human protein-coding gene / receptor tyrosine kinase

disease_links.evidence: EGFR exon 19 deletions, exon 21 L858R, and T790M define treatment-relevant NSCLC subgroups in FDA/NCI sources.

why: Multiple FDA-approved EGFR-directed therapies exist in NSCLC.
FDA-approved companion diagnostics select EGFR-mutant patients.
Best evidence is for EGFR Ex19del and L858R; additional activity exists for T790M.

candidate_drugs.name: osimertinib
candidate_drugs.fit: preferred EGFR TKI for EGFR-mutant NSCLC
candidate_drugs.relevance: Approved for adjuvant, first-line, and T790M-positive metastatic NSCLC; strongest fit for Ex19del/L858R and acquired resistance T790M.

candidate_drugs.name: amivantamab + lazertinib
candidate_drugs.fit: first-line targeted regimen for common EGFR-mutant advanced NSCLC
candidate_drugs.relevance: FDA approved for locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with EGFR Ex19del or L858R; relevant when targeting EGFR-driven disease with a combination strategy.

candidate_drugs.name: amivantamab + carboplatin/pemetrexed
candidate_drugs.relevance: FDA approved for EGFR Ex19del/L858R NSCLC after progression on an EGFR TKI; this is a strong option once resistance emerges.

candidate_drugs.name: erlotinib / gefitinib / afatinib
candidate_drugs.relevance: Still evidence of tractability and historical clinical validation in EGFR-mutant metastatic NSCLC; generally less preferred than osimertinib.

result.bottom_line: Yes. EGFR is a viable and highly targetable lung-cancer driver when NSCLC carries actionable EGFR mutations; the strongest evidence is for Ex19del, L858R, and T790M.
